sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a house in Springfield, MO?
sections.html:
Greene County does. Springfield is the county seat, and the Greene County Assessor values the property, the County Clerk calculates the levies, and the Collector of Revenue bills and collects the tax. Cities, schools, fire districts and the state are among the taxing entities whose levies feed into the one statement the county sends.

  • Assessor: Greene County Assessor Brent Johnson, 940 N. Boonville Avenue, Room 35, phone (417) 868-4101 for real estate.
  • Collector of Revenue: Allen Icet, Room 109 of the Historic Courthouse, phone (417) 868-4036, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • County Clerk: keeps the tax rates and serves as secretary to the Board of Equalization, (417) 829-6244.

The county's Public Access website answers most questions about a parcel's ownership, taxing district and school district, and it is updated nightly.

sections.h2: What is Springfield, and how does that shape its housing market?
sections.html:
Springfield is the third most populous city in Missouri and the largest city in the Ozarks. The Census Bureau estimates 169,847 residents for July 1, 2025, and the city covers about 82 square miles on the Springfield Plateau. Health care, manufacturing, retail, education and tourism drive the economy, and Wikipedia lists CoxHealth and Mercy as the largest employers, with Bass Pro Shops, O'Reilly Auto Parts and Jack Henry headquartered here.

Missouri State University, Drury University, Evangel University and Ozarks Technical Community College are all in or around downtown Springfield. The city is run by a council and a city manager, with eight council members and a mayor serving four-year terms.

sections.h2: When are Springfield property taxes due, and what happens if I pay late?
sections.html:
Real estate and personal property taxes in Springfield are due on December 31 each year. The Collector's notice for the 2025 bills said payments postmarked after that date carry a 9 percent penalty and 2 percent interest, and that a bank check must carry a USPS postmark of December 31 or earlier. The 2026 cycle works the same way, so watch for the statement in mid-November and email collectorhelp@greenecountymo.gov if none arrives by Thanksgiving.

  • Pay online at CountyCollector.com, by bank check through the mail, in person in Room 109 of the Historic Courthouse at 940 N. Boonville Avenue, or by phone.
  • The Collector's page lists processor fees of $1.00 for e-check, 1.5 percent for debit and 2.3 percent for credit cards (2.00 minimum).
  • A drop box is in the courthouse hallway during business hours through December 31.
  • If more than one year is owed, the oldest year must be paid first.

Taxes become delinquent on January 1, and late fees and interest apply from that date. The Collector's office closes on Thanksgiving Day and the day after, so do not leave an in-person payment for that week.

sections.h2: How does selling a house in Springfield change who pays the tax?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property, not the owner. The Collector's real estate FAQ says that if a property changes hands, the current owner is responsible for making sure taxes are paid, and the office does not prorate bills. In most cases the closing company credits the seller's share to the buyer, so check your closing statement.

If a lender collects taxes through an escrow account, the loan company receives the statement and pays it. If the lender fails to pay by mid-December, the statement is remailed to the owner with an extension. You do not have to tell the Collector when a mortgage is paid off, but the mailing address on file with the Assessor must be correct.

  • Ask the title company for the amount owed for the current year and any past years before you set a closing date.
  • Confirm the owner name on the Assessor's record matches the deed of record.
  • Keep the paid receipt; online payments post and the receipt can be downloaded from the Collector's website.

sections.h2: How do I challenge my Springfield assessment?
sections.html:
The Assessor reassesses real estate as of January 1 of each odd-numbered year, so 2027 is the next reassessment. The Assessor mails value change notices before June, and in 2025 they went out the second full week of May. Only owners whose assessed value went up receive one.

  • Step one: an informal conversation with an appraiser, using the dates and phone lines printed on the notice, or the Assessor's informal appeal form for real property.
  • Step two: a formal appeal to the Greene County Board of Equalization through the County Clerk. Forms had to be received by the second Monday in July, which was July 13 in 2026, so that window has closed.
  • Step three: an appeal to the Missouri State Tax Commission at 573-751-2414.

The Board has eight members: three appointed by the Greene County Commission and five by the City of Springfield. It meets on the second Tuesday of each month to certify corrections to the tax book, and hears formal appeals each July at the Historic Courthouse, Room 212. It can raise, lower or sustain a value. Remember that the assessed value only sets the base; the tax equals assessed value times the district levy divided by 100, so a levy increase can raise the bill even when the value does not change.

sections.h2: What relief programs and tax sale rules apply in Springfield?
sections.html:
Greene County runs a Senior Tax Credit on real estate taxes for eligible senior homeowners. First-time applicants can enroll from January 2 through June 30 each year, and approved participants no longer need to renew annually unless ownership or occupancy changes. Participants with delinquent real estate taxes on June 30 are removed from the program, and the credit does not move the December 31 due date.

Unpaid taxes can lead to a tax sale. Greene County offers properties at an annual sale on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. A property qualifies if it owes at least two years of taxes on May 1, and all delinquent taxes must be paid to remove it from the sale. The Collector mails a Notice of Impending Sale in April, and from July 1 only certified funds are accepted for payment.

If you are behind and planning to sell, contact the Collector early and ask for the exact payoff.

sections.h2: What city rules affect owners selling or renting in Springfield?
sections.html:
Springfield regulates short-term rentals, defined as rentals under 30 consecutive days, and requires registration and licensing under City Code Section 36-473. Type 1 covers operator-occupied homes and needs an annual business license. Type 2 covers non-operator-occupied homes in single-family and townhouse districts, requires a permit and a neighborhood meeting, and is not allowed within 500 feet of another Type 2. Type 2 application fees are $715 for planning, $30 for inspection plus the business license.

A buyer who wants to run a short-term rental should ask the city whether the address qualifies. Zoning also limits unrelated occupants to three in single-family districts and four in multi-family districts.

faqs.q: When are Springfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31 each year. Greene County's 2025 notice said payments after that date carry a 9 percent penalty and 2 percent interest, and mailed payments need a postmark of December 31 or earlier.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Springfield property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Greene County Collector of Revenue at (417) 868-4036 about payments, or the Assessor at (417) 868-4101 about the value. The Collector's office is in Room 109 of the Historic Courthouse.

faqs.q: Does the county prorate property tax when I sell my house in Springfield?
faqs.a: No. The Collector's office does not prorate bills, so the closing company usually credits the seller's share to the buyer. Check your closing documents.

faqs.q: Has the deadline to appeal my Springfield assessment passed?
faqs.a: Yes for 2026. Appeal forms had to reach the County Clerk by July 13, 2026. The county reassesses in odd-numbered years, so the next cycle is 2027.

faqs.q: When does Greene County hold its tax sale?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. Properties owing at least two years of taxes on May 1 qualify.
